register.parish: Not visible. The file name says Cicarovce (Čičarovce, Hungarian Csicser, Ung county).

fields.note: Written above the entry. The third digit is cramped; the next entry's year is a clear 1882 and the file name agrees.
The ditto-like strokes beside it fill the unused sub-columns.
gk. = görög katolikus. gazda = a peasant holding his own land.

Surname only. Could also be read Emrgovich or Cmrgovich. Needs another entry in the same hand.

translation: No. 36. 1882. Born 19 August, baptised 20 August: Mihály, a boy, legitimate. Parents: György Demkó, Greek Catholic, farmer, and Mária Hreskó, Roman Catholic. Residence: Viszoka, house no. 132. Godparents: Mihály Varga, Roman Catholic, and Anna Hreskó, Roman Catholic. Baptised by Csurgovich (reading uncertain). No remarks.
notes: The image is a strip 157 pixels high. No page header, parish name, page number or film number is visible, so the register is identified only by the collector's file name.
The entry above (no. 35) and the one below are partly visible and name other families; they are not transcribed.
The child was born at Viszoka, not at Čičarovce. If the label is right, Čičarovce is where the book was kept.

Added at DM-B-003 on a second look: the entry below, of which only the top line shows, has the residence 'Vaján' (Vojany) and the officiant 'Polányi Endre'. Two different priests officiate on one page.

title: Petition to the bishop for leave to build a wooden chapel, 27 January 1803, page 1

fields.original: Conspiciendo nosmet ipsos tam miseram, et non stabilem Capellam habere, ideo supplices ad Dominum Nostrum Terrestrem Antonium K. Mihályi concurrimus, qui etiam videndo rectam nostram petitionem, nobis locum pro capella in proprio fundo donavit, quemadmodum ejus Manuscriptum hic involutum exhibet. Ideo nunc unice ad Excellentiam Vestram Praesuleam devotissimi veniendo flexis genibus oramus, quatenus gratioso indultu Excellentiae Vestrae, in eodem loco donato, ligneam Capellam nobis exstruere valeremus. In reliquo Altissimis Praesularibus Gratiis nos commendantes perseveramus Excellentiae Vestrae Praesuleae
fields.english: Seeing that we have so poor and unsound a chapel, we went as petitioners to our landlord, Antonius K. Mihályi, who found our request just and gave us a site for a chapel on his own land, as his enclosed note shows. We now come most humbly to Your Episcopal Excellency alone and beg on bended knee that, by Your Excellency's gracious leave, we may build ourselves a wooden chapel on the site so given. Commending ourselves to your episcopal favour, we remain Your Excellency's
fields.note: Abbreviations expanded. The landlord's name is read 'K. Mihályi'; the initial is not expanded.
'Tegy.' taken as Tegenye, a village beside Pálócz. Identification from training; flagged to the Places agent.

fields.original: Georgius Kicska, Haiduk Joannes, Stanko Joannes, Petrus Joannes et reliqui incolae Palocziensis
fields.english: Georgius Kicska, Joannes Haiduk, Joannes Stanko, Joannes Petrus and the other inhabitants of Pálócz (Pavlovce nad Uhom)
fields.note: Surnames Kicska and Petrus are doubtful readings.

fields.original: Michael Ochmir, Georgius Feterik, et reliqui incolae Tegenyienses
fields.english: Michael Ochmir, Georgius Feterik and the other inhabitants of Tegenye
fields.note: Both surnames doubtful.

translation: To the bishop. The people of Pálócz, Tegenye, Viszoka and Mogyorós say their chapel is poor and unsound. Their landlord, Antonius K. Mihályi, has given them a site on his own land, and they ask the bishop's leave to build a wooden chapel there. Signed at Tegenye on 27 January 1803 by named men of each village 'and the other inhabitants'. The names for Viszoka and Mogyorós are on the second page (DM-D-003).
notes: All names are in one hand: the scribe wrote them, the villagers did not sign.
No archive stamp, fond or folio number is visible on this page.
The addressee is not named. 'Praesul' is a bishop; the four villages and the request for a wooden chapel fit a petition from Greek Catholics to the bishop of Mukachevo. That is an inference.

title: Petition to the bishop, 27 January 1803, page 2: signers for Viszoka and Mogyorós

fields.original: Michael Hrabik, Andreas Ivanov, Joannes Pikulics, Joannes Demko et reliqui incolae Possessionis Viszoka
fields.english: Michael Hrabik, Andreas Ivanov, Joannes Pikulics, Joannes Demko and the other inhabitants of the village of Viszoka
fields.note: 'Joannes Demko' and 'Viszoka' are clear. Hrabik, Ivanov and Pikulics are doubtful.

fields.original: Joannes Darilo, Basilius Borisza et reliqui incolae possessionis Mogyorós
fields.english: Joannes Darilo, Basilius Borisza and the other inhabitants of the village of Mogyorós (Liesková)
fields.note: Darilo may be Davilo.

translation: Continuation of the signatures: four named men of Viszoka, the last of them Joannes Demko, and two of Mogyorós, each group 'and the other inhabitants'.
notes: Photo metadata: taken 19 Feb 2020 with a phone, location tag 48.207 N, 22.644 E, which is in Berehove, Ukraine. A branch of the Zakarpattia state archive is in that town (from training, to be confirmed by the Places agent). This is the only provenance the files carry.
The earliest Demko at Viszoka on paper so far: 79 years before the 1882 baptism at house 132.

title: Baptism register entry no. 44: Mária, daughter of Mihály Demkó and Anna, born 24 February, year not shown
kind: Parish baptism register, one entry cut from a page

fields.note: Five narrow columns hold ditto marks, a stroke and a short word. Without the column headings they cannot be assigned.
The rite abbreviation after the name is unclear. zsellér = a cottar, a peasant without a holding.
Surname begins with an ornate L or B: Latnoszki, Batronszki and Latvoszki are all possible.

translation: No. 44. Born 24 February, baptised 27 February: Mária. Father Mihály Demkó, cottar. Mother Anna, surname uncertain. The strip is cut before the residence, godparents and priest, and shows no year or parish.
notes: The collector's own label says 'maybe'.

It disagrees with the civil record DM-D-008 on the day of birth (24 February against 22 August) and on the mother (Anna against Mária Kocsis). It is a different child unless the year proves otherwise. See DM-H-015.

title: Notarial deed of sale, 1966, one page: declaration that Mike Duska married once, to Maria Demko, who died 9 September 1950
collector_label: Maria Demko Notarial Document Regarding Guardianship of [name withheld] - establishes date of death

fields.original: THAT all taxes and assessments, both general and special, imposed upon the said immoveable, have been paid to the First day of November, Nineteen Hundred and Sixty-six;

THAT the said Mike Duska was married but once, namely, to the late Dame Maria Demko, who died at the City of Montreal, on the Ninth day of September, Nineteen Hundred and Fifty, and that he has not remarried since the date of the death of his late said wife.
THAT the present sale shall be effective as of the First day of November, Nineteen Hundred and Sixty-six.
By virtue of these presents, the Purchaser shall become the absolute owner of the immoveable hereby sold, with immediate possession thereof [...]
fields.note: The page ends in the second condition.

translation: A page from a deed of sale of a property, effective 1 November 1966. The seller declares that Mike Duska married only once, to Maria Demko, that she died in Montréal on 9 September 1950, and that he has not remarried.
notes: Only this page was given. The notary, the parties, the property and the deed number are on other pages.
The file name speaks of a guardianship and names a living person; that name is withheld here and in the archived file name. Nothing on this page concerns a guardianship.
Mike Duska was alive on the date of the deed.

translation: Entry 45, page 320. Registered at Alsókánya on 23 August 1906. The father came in person and is known to the registrar: Mihály Demkó, Greek Catholic, agricultural day-labourer, living at Solymos, born at Magasrév, aged 24. The mother: his wife, born Mária Kocsis, Greek Catholic, living and born at Solymos, aged 20. The child, a girl, Greek Catholic, named Mária, was born at Solymos on 22 August 1906 at nine in the morning. The entry was read out and explained in Slovak, approved and signed by the registrar and by Mihály Demkó.
notes: A state register on printed security paper, made the day after the birth on the father's own word: an original record with a first-hand informant.
The image is a phone screenshot of a scan, dated 13 Jan 2022 in its metadata. The register's custodian, district and volume are not shown.
The father signs his own name. In 1882 terms he is the right age to the week: a Mihály Demkó born at Viszoka on 19 August 1882 turned 24 four days before this entry.
House numbers are not asked for on this form.

translation: Certificate no. 106 of 1947 from the Roman Catholic parish of Senné, citing volume IV, page 110, entry 43 of 1929: Štefan, male, legitimate, born 21 October and baptised 26 October 1929. Father Michal Duska, Roman Catholic, cottar, of Senné. Mother Maria Demko, Greek Catholic, of Iňačovce. Residence Senné no. 160. Godparents Jozef Macko-Kocák (?) of Michalovce and Juliana Hanušcák (?), wife of Ján Bandura (?), of Senné. Baptised by Ján Barna, parish priest. Issued at Senné on 19 August 1947 under the parish seal.
notes: A derivative: an extract made 18 years after the baptism from the parish's own book, with volume and page cited.
A son of a Roman Catholic father and Greek Catholic mother, entered in the Roman Catholic book.
The mother's maiden surname and home village are given in the form used for a wife of another rite: 'gr.kat., Iňačovce'.
Shared with the Duska agent's line (Ahn 4 and Ahn 8).
